responsibilities: Engage with business users and stakeholders to thoroughly understand their reporting needs, data-related challenges, and translate these into clear analytics requirements.
Analyse existing processes, data sources, and reporting solutions to identify areas for enhancement and provide well-considered recommendations for improvement.
Contribute actively to solution design by mapping out data flows, models, ETL processes, reporting structures, and BI solutions that align with organisational objectives.
Work collaboratively with technical teams to assess feasibility, dependencies, impacts, and implementation considerations for proposed solutions.
Support the refinement and prioritisation of requirements to ensure all delivered solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned with business goals.
Extract and analyse data from core business systems such as CRM, ERP, or operational platforms using SQL or other appropriate methods.
Validate data accuracy, completeness, consistency; identify gaps or anomalies; resolve issues at source in partnership with relevant technical teams.
Design, develop, maintain ETL processes that transform raw data into clean, structured datasets ready for business use; monitor performance and optimise pipelines.
Support the maintenance of centralised data platforms or warehouses by designing schemas that facilitate efficient analytics; coordinate changes resulting from system updates.
Develop dashboards and reports based on stakeholder requirements; translate complex information into clear visualisations; continuously improve reporting solutions based on feedback.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Understanding of data quality management practices including governance standards and security principles ensures reliable outputs
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD emphasizes data accuracy, validation, governance and reliability with no velocity/speed language, coding as rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: extract data from various enterprise systems... resolve issues at source
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The JD is generic about the actual business sector (agency-anonymized posting) and describes standard BI/reporting consequences without financial-reporting or regulatory override language, so moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Maintaining centralised data platforms or warehouses will be part of your remit-ensuring schemas are optimised for analytics
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The role maintains and extends an existing centralised data platform rather than building one from scratch, and tools are named in a fix/scale context, indicating mid-stage maturity.
evidence.jd_authorship: extract data from various enterprise systems using advanced SQL techniques or APIs, validate its quality and consistency, then transform it through robust ETL processes
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: This is an agency-anonymized posting ("A leading organisation") written in generic boilerplate language that could apply to almost any data analytics engineering role, with no company-specific scale numbers or precise tool names.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Engage with business users and stakeholders to thoroughly understand their reporting needs
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The JD describes generic 'business users' and 'stakeholders' across the company without naming a dominant functional audience, so mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: Support the refinement and prioritisation of requirements to ensure all delivered solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned with business goals
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role primarily supports and translates stakeholder requirements rather than setting direction, an execution framing.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tool usage or AI-infrastructure-building expectation appears anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: A solid grasp of data quality management practices ensures your outputs are reliable
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality is mentioned as a desired background/practice in requirements without an explicit ownership verb framing it as something the candidate defines or owns.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Validate data accuracy, completeness, consistency; identify gaps or anomalies; resolve issues at source
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: There is repeated emphasis on data accuracy and reliability, but it is secondary to the overall delivery/BI-solution framing rather than dominant, so moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Support the maintenance of centralised data platforms or warehouses by designing schemas that facilitate efficient analytics; coordinate changes resulting from system updates
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role maintains and optimises existing data platforms and pipelines rather than building new infrastructure from scratch.
evidence.loss_aversion: Validate data accuracy, completeness, consistency; identify gaps or anomalies; resolve issues at source — a moderate reliability concern rather than a dominant compliance/regulatory risk register.
